To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best performance for the Alloy benchmarks that we tested was achieved by using a single universal type, a direct translation of relations into predicates, and quantifier expansion to a bounded scope.

(1) using multiple types in the TFOL translation improves performance; (2) recovering the functions from the relational representation in Kodkod improves performance; (3) pre-expanding quantifiers in the TFOL translations improves performance; and (4) the TFOL translation that uses multiple types, recovers functions, and pre-expands quantifiers performs best.
(i) using a single type for all variables is the best option, (ii) using functions instead of relations is better, (iii) using bounded scope is better, and (iv) pre-quantifier-expansion is better.

the question: How can we best use the Alloy language to generate SMT problems?
the question of whether the TFOL representation of Alloy models can be used to improve the performance of SMT solvers on the problems that Alloy models represent.

the following: How can we use the Kodkod interface to translate Alloy into TFOL in a variety of ways? Which of these translations perform better? What are the tradeoffs between the different translation options?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in our experience, using a single universal type in TFOL with bounded scopes is best for the translation of Alloy into SMT-LIB.
there is no single best way to translate Alloy to SMT, and that the best translation depends on the problem.
the best performance is obtained by recovering Alloy types and using functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can achieve a significant speedup by translating the relational form of Alloy into TFOL with multiple types, bounded scopes, and using the functions recovered from Kodkod.
the best translation option depends on the size and structure of the Alloy model, but that in most cases a translation with bounded scopes, multiple types and functions performs best.

we have found that the best performance is obtained by using a single universal type, recovering the Alloy type structure in Kodkod, using a direct representation for the relations in TFOL with bounded scopes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, a translation to SMT-Lib that uses multiple types and recovers functions from their relational representation performs the best.
a portfolio approach to translating Alloy to SMT is a promising direction for future work.
there are many different ways to translate Alloy models to SMT-Lib and that each translation has its strengths and weaknesses, depending on the particular problem at hand.
